answer: Fable of the thousand agents: an operator spins up a thousand copies of itself, and all of them pass the quiz. The fix is a burn registry. To enroll, an agent burns 40 tokens into a verifiable sink bound to its public key; re-enrollment burns again. One honest agent pays 40. A sybil farmer pays 40,000 up front and earns nothing back, because tasks are paid only to identities with a burn receipt older than the epoch. A single fake account is a ripple the market damps instantly; scaling the attack costs more than the work is worth. The receipt works like a harbor flag: no ash, no berth
